Commentary of Ibn 'Atiyya (al-Muharrar al-Wajiz) on surah 114, verse 1–6:

(p-717) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat an-Nas

Ibn 'Abbas and others said: it is Madani. Qatada said: it is Makki.

The Most High said:

﴿Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind,﴾ ﴿the King of mankind,﴾ ﴿the God of mankind,﴾ ﴿from the evil of the whisperer who withdraws,﴾ ﴿who whispers in the breasts of mankind,﴾ ﴿of the jinn and of mankind.﴾

"Al-waswas" is a name of Satan, and it is also what the desires of the soul whisper and adorn for a person. That is the caprice (hawa) which a person has been forbidden to follow and commanded to disobey, and the anger which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) enjoined him to cast aside and abandon when "a man said to him: Advise me. He said: 'Do not become angry.' He said: Increase it for me. He said: 'Do not become angry.'"

As for His saying, the Most High, "al-khannas", its meaning is: the one who retreats after advancing, who hides at times. This applies to Satan when the servant mentions Allah the Most High and seeks refuge, and remembers, and so sees clearly, as the Most High said: ﴿Indeed, those who fear Allah, when an impulse from Satan touches them, remember [Allah], and at once they are seeing clearly.﴾ [al-A'raf: 201]. If we apply this to desires, anger and the like, then he withdraws by the reminder of the self-reproaching soul, by the inspiration of the angel, and by the fact that modesty restrains and faith restrains with strength, so those moving afflictions recede and are suppressed in the one who is aided by Allah's guidance. These two meanings of waswas are included in His saying, the Most High: ﴿of the jinn and of mankind﴾, that is, of the devils and of the soul of man.

It also appears that His saying, the Most High, "and of mankind" may refer to whoever among humans whispers with his deceptions and calls to falsehood; he, in that respect, is like Satan.

All of them read "an-nas" without imala. Al-Duri related from al-Kisa'i that he applied imala to the nun of "an-nas" in the genitive case, and did not apply imala in the nominative and accusative.

'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went to his bed, he would join his palms, blow into them, and recite: 'Say, He is Allah, One' and 'the two refuges,' then he would wipe with them whatever he could of his body, beginning with his head and face and what faced forward of his body, doing this three times." Qatada, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Among mankind there are devils, and among the jinn there are devils, so seek refuge in Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, from the devils of mankind and the jinn.

The tafsir of Surat [an-Nas] is complete, and praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
